## Round 531: SECRMAN confirmed clean; RPC-delivery mechanism fully traced - explains why IOP thread scheduling never affected it (task #447)

**SECRMAN (real module #27 of 29, flagged in Round 530) reviewed against its real source (`secrman.c`, 1380 lines).** Its real `_start()` is simple: `RegisterLibraryEntries(&_exp_secrman)` (a LOADCORE library call this project's module loader already handles implicitly via static ELF-parse-time export registration, not by executing real LOADCORE code for it), then two purely-local calls (`ResetMcHandlers()`, `RegisterSecrCallbackHandlers()`) that only set internal callback-pointer state - no `CreateThread`/`CreateSema`/`WaitSema`/any thread-related syscall anywhere in its init path. This confirms (does not newly discover) Round 529's finding: SECRMAN, like every module 22-28 except REBOOT, does not touch `iop_hle_thread.c`'s dispatch path during front-loaded init - fully consistent with, and no exception to, the already-established picture. No gap found; no fix needed.

**Major architectural clarification: traced exactly how this project's RPC-delivery counters (`g_r303_rpc_pending_sets`/`g_r303_rpc_delivered_count`, the ones tracked across Rounds 526-529) actually work, and why IOP thread-scheduling state never affected them.** Read `source/core/ee/ee_core.c`'s full RPC-delivery machinery (`ee_arm_rpc_bind_pending()`, `ee_arm_rpc_call_pending()`, `ee_check_rpc_bind_pending()`, and the Round 347 CDVD-NCMD real-dispatch re-entry path) end to end:

- Every real EE-side `SifBindRpc()`/`SifCallRpc()` request arms a **fixed 200-slice countdown timer** (`g_rpc_bind_delay = 200`, reduced from 50000 in Round 248 purely for host-native survey throughput) via `ee_arm_rpc_bind_pending()`/`ee_arm_rpc_call_pending()`. This timer is decremented unconditionally, once per EE step, by `ee_check_rpc_bind_pending()` - **it does not consult IOP thread state, module-loader completion, or any IOP-side execution at all.** When it reaches zero, `sif_cmd_iop_send_rpc_bind_rend()` synthesizes the reply packet directly. This is the mechanism generating essentially all 228 of the counted RPC deliveries in every survey run to date, and it fully explains Round 529's finding that retiring-vs-not-retiring IOP thread 1 produced byte-for-byte identical RPC growth curves: **the counted mechanism was never coupled to IOP execution in the first place.**
- There IS a real, genuine exception, already built in Round 347: `ee_try_cdvd_ncmd_real_dispatch()` intercepts `SIF_SID_CDVD_NCMD` RPC *calls* whose `rpc_number` maps defensibly to one of 7 real NCMD MMIO opcodes (`CD_NCMD_READ`/`DVDREAD`/`SEEK`/`STANDBY`/`STOP`/`PAUSE`/`GETTOC`). For those specific calls (and only those), this project performs a **real** `iop_cdvd_mmio_write8(...NCMD...)` - genuinely triggering `dispatch_ncmd()` and real IOP-side CDVDMAN interrupt-handler execution (via the real, already-registered IRQ2 handler, Round 338's citation) - and defers the EE reply until `ee_check_cdvd_ncmd_pending()` observes that handler's completion via `iop_hle_intr_get_handler_completion_count(2)`, a genuine asynchronous, IOP-execution-gated completion. (Even this path's *final* reply delivery still funnels through the same `ee_arm_rpc_call_pending()` used everywhere else - so a real dispatch, if it ever fires, would still show up as one of the counted RPC deliveries, just gated on real IOP work first instead of a flat 200-slice timer.)
- **This closes the loop with this project's own long-standing, independently-reconfirmed finding that `dispatch_ncmd()`'s call count has stayed at 0 across every survey since Round 90** (Rounds 90-92, 269-274, 337, 361-365, 397, 455, 470, 498 all separately measured this). Given `ee_try_cdvd_ncmd_real_dispatch()` is the *only* path that can ever increment that counter, and it requires a `SIF_SID_CDVD_NCMD` **CALL** (not BIND) with one of the 7 specific mapped `rpc_number`s, the fact that it has never fired across 40M+ slices of organic boot in any round means: **OSDSYS's disc-browser has never yet issued one of those specific real disc-command RPC calls** - not because IOP-side dispatch is broken (it demonstrably works when driven directly, and this round confirms its trigger condition is real and correctly wired), but because the EE-side application logic that would need to issue that first real disc command has never reached that decision point. This is exactly the same conclusion this project's much earlier rounds (90-92, 269-274, 361-365, 397, 480-498) already converged on from the EE/OSDSYS-disassembly side - **this round supplies the missing architectural other-half of that picture**: it's not merely that OSDSYS "hasn't asked yet," it's that the IOP-side machinery that would answer for real, if asked, sits idle and unexercised the entire time, and no amount of IOP-side thread-scheduling work (Rounds 512-529) could ever have surfaced or fixed this, because the gap has always been squarely on the EE/OSDSYS application-logic side, not the IOP dispatch side. This matches task #447's own original Round 90-92 framing exactly, now re-derived independently via a completely different investigative path (IOP thread scheduling -> RPC delivery architecture) and landing on the same conclusion - strong convergent evidence, not a new open question.

**Classification:** docs-only round - no tracked source changed.

## Round 532: real ps2sdk CDVD-NCMD client library reviewed - DISKREADY-gate hypothesis formed and empirically refuted (task #447)

Per the user's confirmation ("yeah") to examine the real `ee/rpc/cdvd/src` client library, reviewed `ncmd.c` from the ps2sdk-master tree (Round 530's ingested source). Found a real, hard gating pattern: every real disc-command wrapper function (`sceCdRead`, `sceCdReadDVDV`, `sceCdReadCDDA`, `sceCdSeek`, `sceCdStandby`, `sceCdStop`, `sceCdPause`) begins with `if (sceCdNCmdDiskReady() == SCECdNotReady) return 0;` before issuing its own real RPC call - and `sceCdNCmdDiskReady()` is itself a real RPC call (`rpc_number = CD_NCMD_DISKREADY = 14`) that returns its reply's raw first word directly, compared against `SCECdNotReady = 6` (real `SCECdvdInterruptCode` enum: `CdlNoIntr=0, CdlDataReady=1, SCECdComplete=2, CdlAcknowledge=3, CdlDataEnd=4, CdlDiskError=5, SCECdNotReady=6`, already cited in Round 475's `SIF_SID_CDVD_DISKREADY` work).

**Hypothesis formed:** this project's `ee_try_cdvd_ncmd_real_dispatch()` (Round 347) only maps `rpc_number` in `{1,3,4,5,6,7,8}` (READ/DVDREAD/GETTOC/SEEK/STANDBY/STOP/PAUSE) to real IOP dispatch - it has no case for `14` (DISKREADY), so any DISKREADY N-command call would fall through to `ee_core.c`'s generic `SIF_SID_CDVD_NCMD` catch-all reply. If that catch-all answered DISKREADY with a value real code interprets as "not ready," it would explain the long-standing `dispatch_ncmd()==0` mystery via a genuine upstream SDK-convention gate.

**Hypothesis checked against the actual code (`ee_core.c` ~line 5086-5148) and empirically refuted, in two independent ways:**

1. **Logically:** the generic catch-all (reached whenever `ee_try_cdvd_ncmd_real_dispatch()` returns 0) writes a single leading result word of `0` into the caller's recvbuf - documented in the Round 347-era comment as "0 = success placeholder," the same convention used for MCSERV/CDVD_INIT above it. `0 != SCECdNotReady (6)`. If a real DISKREADY call ever reached this path, `sceCdNCmdDiskReady()` would return `0`, the caller's `== SCECdNotReady` check would evaluate false, and the real disc-command wrapper would proceed *past* its own gate - the opposite of blocking. This mechanism cannot be the cause of the observed stall even in principle.
2. **Empirically:** built a scratch-instrumented copy of `ee_core.c` (`/tmp/r532_ee_core_instrumented.c`, tracked source untouched) adding a `rpc_number` histogram at the `SIF_SID_CDVD_NCMD` entry point, linked against the other 37 cached real project objects, and ran a fresh 40,000,000-slice organic boot (real US BIOS + real Tekken Tag Tournament Demo disc). Result: `SIF_SID_CDVD_NCMD` is entered exactly **once** in the entire run, with `rpc_number=10` (`CD_NCMD_CDDASTREAM`, exactly matching Round 473's already-documented finding) - and it is **never** entered with `rpc_number=14` (DISKREADY) or any of the other mapped values. `rpc_bind_sets=228`/`rpc_delivered=228`, matching the long-established baseline exactly (no regression, confirms the instrumentation is inert).

**Conclusion:** the DISKREADY-gate hypothesis is refuted at the root - not merely "the reply value happens to be safe," but "the call this project's fallback would mishandle is never issued in the first place." This tightens, rather than reopens, Round 531's synthesis: OSDSYS's disc-browser never issues *any* real gated NCMD command (READ/SEEK/DISKREADY/etc.) on this boot path - the single real NCMD traffic observed across every survey to date remains the one CDDASTREAM-init call (Round 473). The real gap remains exactly where Rounds 90-92/269-274/361-365/480-498/531 already converged: OSDSYS's own EE-side application logic never reaches the decision point that would issue a real disc-command RPC, not any IOP-side dispatch defect or reply-value bug. No source fix is warranted from this round's finding - there is nothing to fix in a code path that is never exercised.

**Classification:** docs-only/diagnostic round - only untracked scratch files (`/tmp/r532_ee_core_instrumented.c`, `/tmp/r532_ncmd_survey.c`) were created; no tracked source changed. Regression suite and Wii rebuild correctly skipped.

**Method 2 - new hypothesis from the real ps2sdk ExecPS2Patch source.** With the interrupt-handler avenue closed, re-read `ee/kernel/src/osdsrc/src/ExecPS2.c` (`ExecPS2Patch()`/`SoftPeripheralEEReset()`, ingested Round 530) against Round 462/463's own already-confirmed-correct disassembly of this exact BIOS (every fixed address in the patch file - `0x800125EC` ThreadID, `0x80017400` TCB base, `0x80004970` CancelWakeupThread, `0x80004288` ChangeThreadPriority, `0x800057E8` p_ExecPS2 - independently matched real disassembly in Round 462/463, unrelated to this patch file at the time). The real mechanism this project's syscall-7 trampoline (Rounds 466-469/502) stands in for does substantially more than a raw PC/register hijack: before jumping to the new program, it walks **every other thread's TCB** and calls `TerminateThread()`+`DeleteThread()` on each non-dormant one, reinitializes semaphores, the PGIF handler, and performs a full `SoftPeripheralEEReset()` (GS/INTC/timer/EE-reset/FPU/scratchpad re-init). This project's trampoline does none of this - it only touches the current thread. New hypothesis: the redirect is the real kernel scheduler naturally rescheduling one of the ~12 real, still-alive OSDSYS threads (task #163's live-PCSX2 citation) once the hijacked thread blocks, yields, or gets preempted - not an interrupt collision at all.

**Test.** Built `/tmp/r533_tcb_terminate_trampoline.c`, extending the established Round 466-469/502 recipe (organic warmup, real `SCED_500.41;1` ELF extraction via `iop_cdvd_disc_find_file`/`iop_cdvd_disc_read_sector`, `ee_elf_load()`, VBLANK-END mask) with one new step immediately before firing the trampoline: read the real current-thread-ID global (`0x800125EC`, confirmed `tid=3`, matching Round 462 exactly), then walk `TCB[1..255]` (`0x80017400 + i*0x4C`, real stride per the fetched struct) and zero `TCB[i].status` (offset `+0x08`) for every non-current thread with a non-zero status - mimicking `TerminateThread`+`DeleteThread`'s net end state. 8 real threads were found alive and cleared (`TCB[1]` status `0x02` READY, `TCB[2]`/`4`-`9` status `0x04` WAIT) - a real, evidenced count, not a guess. Ran 60,000,000 further slices in sampled chunks (matching Round 502's scale).

**Result 2 - refutes this round's own new hypothesis.** The redirect into OSDSYS's resting-loop address family (`0x8000CCA0`, `0x8000CFF4`, `0x8000F870`, `0x8000CFD0`, `0x8000CC9C`, `0x8000CFF0`, `0x8000F86C` - the exact same `0x8000CFxx`/`0x8000CCxx`/`0x8000F8xx` family Round 466/469/502 already documented) still happens, on the same rough timescale as Round 502's un-terminated run. Zeroing `TCB.status` for the other threads did not prevent it. This is a genuine, evidenced negative result, not a null run - the termination loop demonstrably executed (8 real threads found and cleared, logged individually).

**Assessment - refined leading hypothesis for a future round.** The most likely explanation for why status-field zeroing alone was insufficient: real `TerminateThread`/`DeleteThread` don't just flip a status flag, they unlink the TCB from the real scheduler's priority-bucketed ready-queue linked list (`TCB.next`/`TCB.prev`, both real fields in the already-fetched struct, not touched by this round's edit). If the real dispatcher's ready-queue walk follows those pointers rather than (or in addition to) checking `status`, a status-zeroed-but-still-linked TCB could still be reached and scheduled. A future round's next concrete step: either call the real `TerminateThread`/`DeleteThread` functions themselves (0x80003e00/0x80003f00, also confirmed-real addresses) as genuine subroutine calls from the trampoline rather than hand-editing state, or trace the real ready-queue head/bucket structure and unlink `TCB.next`/`prev` directly. A second, equally plausible non-bug explanation not yet ruled out: Tekken Tag Tournament Demo's own attract-mode/timeout logic may legitimately call back into OSDSYS after a period with no real save/config presence - this project's trampoline provides no real memory card and no further pad input during the post-trampoline window, which is exactly the condition under which a real demo disc's own timeout-to-browser behavior would fire. Both explanations remain open for a future round.

**Classification.** Diagnostic round - only untracked scratch files (`/tmp/r533_ee_core_instrumented.c`, `/tmp/r533_intc_survey.c`, `/tmp/r533_tcb_terminate_trampoline.c`) were created; no tracked source changed. Regression suite and Wii rebuild correctly skipped.

## Round 534: real TerminateThread/DeleteThread subroutine calls confirm proper cleanup - but the redirect still happens, refuting the thread-termination hypothesis rigorously (task #447)

Direct, more rigorous follow-up to Round 533's refuted hand-edit experiment. Round 533's TCB.status-zeroing approach left open one honest caveat: real `TerminateThread`/`DeleteThread` unlink the TCB from the scheduler's ready-queue linked list (`TCB.next`/`TCB.prev`), which a direct status-field write does not touch - so Round 533's negative result was not fully conclusive on its own.

**Method.** Extended `/tmp/r533_tcb_terminate_trampoline.c` into `/tmp/r534_real_terminate_trampoline.c`: instead of writing `TCB.status = 0` directly, this round performs genuine synthetic subroutine calls into the real, confirmed-correct BIOS code at `0x80003e00` (`TerminateThread`) and `0x80003f00` (`DeleteThread`) - setting `$a0` to the thread ID and `$ra` to a controlled sentinel address in scratchpad, jumping `$pc` to the real function, then single-stepping (`ee_core_step()`) until `$pc` returns to the sentinel. This runs the real machine code with its real side effects (including whatever ready-queue unlinking it performs), in the same live register/stack context already established by the organic boot - not a guess at what the function does, the function's own real bytes execute.

**Result.** All 16 real subroutine calls (`TerminateThread`+`DeleteThread` for each of the 8 real non-current, non-dormant threads found - TCB[1,2,4,5,6,7,8,9]) completed cleanly and quickly: `TerminateThread` returned after 78-92 real EE instructions, `DeleteThread` after 48, for every thread, with no timeout and no halt. Each thread's `TCB.status` read back as `0x00000000` afterward, confirmed by direct memory read. This is real, verified, correct execution of the actual cleanup code - the most faithful reproduction of `ExecPS2Patch()`'s thread-teardown step this project has built.

**Despite this, the redirect into OSDSYS's resting-loop address family still happens.** A 40,000,000-slice post-trampoline run (10 sampled 4,000,000-slice chunks) shows `ee_pc` cycling through the same `0x8000CCxx`/`0x8000CFxx`/`0x8000F8xx` family documented since Round 466 (`0x8000CC88`, `0x8000CCB8`, `0x8000CFF4`, `0x8000CE44`, `0x8000F814`, `0x8000CFD0`, `0x8000CC84`, `0x8000CCB4`, `0x8000CFF0`, `0x8000CE40`) on essentially the same timescale as both Round 502 (no thread cleanup) and Round 533 (status-only cleanup). GS state is unchanged (`PMODE=0x66`, `DISPFB2=0x1400`, non-zero `DISPLAY2` - same rendering circuit-2 state as every prior round in this thread).

**Conclusion - the thread-termination hypothesis is now refuted rigorously, not just tentatively.** With real subroutine calls confirmed to execute correctly and fully clean up every other thread's real kernel state, and the redirect still occurring on the same timescale, stale OSDSYS threads are not the cause either. Combined with Round 533's AddIntcHandler census (no stale interrupt handler exists), this closes out both of this investigative arc's two concrete, evidenced hypotheses. The two remaining open explanations, neither yet tested: (a) this is genuine, correct Tekken Tag Tournament Demo attract-mode/timeout-to-browser behavior given the trampoline provides no ongoing pad input or memory card presence signal after the initial CROSS press, or (b) some other real kernel/hardware state this trampoline still doesn't replicate (candidates: the real `SoftPeripheralEEReset()`'s INTC re-init with mask `0xdffd` - not attempted this round, since Round 533's census showed no OTHER handler is registered, making a full INTC re-init unlikely to matter - or something entirely outside the ExecPS2Patch citation's scope).

**Classification.** Diagnostic round - only untracked scratch files (`/tmp/r534_real_terminate_trampoline.c`) were created; no tracked source changed. Regression suite and Wii rebuild correctly skipped.

Direct test of the last untested explanation from Round 534: that the redirect into OSDSYS's resting loop might be genuine, correct Tekken Tag Tournament Demo attract-mode/timeout-to-browser behavior, since every trampoline test since Round 457 presses CROSS once during warmup and then provides no further pad input for the entire post-trampoline window.

**Method.** Extended `/tmp/r534_real_terminate_trampoline.c` into `/tmp/r535_pad_input_trampoline.c`: identical recipe (organic warmup, real disc ELF extraction, VBLANK-END mask, real `TerminateThread`/`DeleteThread` subroutine calls for all other threads, syscall-7 trampoline), but this round presses and releases CROSS at the start of every one of the 10 post-trampoline sampled chunks, so real pad input keeps arriving throughout the entire 40,000,000-slice observation window instead of stopping after the initial press.

**Result - exact match to Round 534, instruction-for-instruction.** Final state: `ee_pc=0x8000CE40 instr=639999321` - identical to Round 534's `ee_pc=0x8000CE40 instr=639999321` (no thread-cleanup difference between the two rounds' trampoline setup, only the pad-input pattern differs). Every sampled chunk's PC and instruction count matches Round 534's chunk-by-chunk trace exactly. Continuous pad input changed nothing whatsoever, not even by a single instruction.

**Assessment.** This is a clean, decisive negative result, stronger than a typical "no effect" finding because of the exact bit-for-bit match - it doesn't just fail to prevent the redirect, it proves the entire post-trampoline execution trace is completely deterministic and totally insensitive to this project's pad-input mechanism, at least in this synthetic single-thread-hijack context. This refutes the attract-mode/timeout hypothesis (continuous real player input would defeat a real timeout-driven return-to-browser, but did not change the outcome). It also raises - without yet answering - a further honest question worth flagging for a future round: does this project's pad-input mechanism actually reach a real, polled input-read code path in this specific post-trampoline context at all, or does the hijacked thread simply never poll the pad hardware during this particular window regardless of what's pressed? Both this round's result and Round 464/510's much earlier, unrelated finding that pad polling isn't a factor in the pre-trampoline idle loop are consistent with pad state genuinely not being consulted anywhere on this code path - not with pad input being consulted-but-ignored.

**Classification.** Diagnostic round - only untracked scratch files (`/tmp/r535_pad_input_trampoline.c`) were created; no tracked source changed. Regression suite and Wii rebuild correctly skipped.


## Round 536: US-BIOS-revision trampoline test - redirect destination is a genuinely different address family (raw BIOS ROM reset-vector region, not OSDSYS's resting loop), but warmup depth differs too much for a clean comparison (task #447)

Direct action on the user's instruction ("go and after that try the bios"): tests whether the redirect-to-BIOS-resting-loop phenomenon documented across Rounds 466-535 (always using the scph10000 Japan BIOS) is specific to that BIOS revision, or a BIOS-general characteristic of the syscall-7 trampoline technique itself.

**Method.** Copied the real, verified-distinct US BIOS (`ps2-0200a-20040614-100909.bin`, MD5 `d333558cc14561c1fdc334c75d5f37b7`, verified Round 503) into place alongside the existing scph10000 Japan BIOS. Built `/tmp/r536_us_bios_trampoline.c` from Round 534's driver, swapping only the BIOS image path and log tags. Deliberately **dropped** Round 534's real `TerminateThread`/`DeleteThread` subroutine-call step for this round: those fixed addresses (`0x80003e00`, `0x80003f00`, plus the TCB base `0x80017400` and ThreadID global `0x800125EC`) were validated specifically against the scph10000 Japan BIOS via Round 462/463's direct disassembly of that exact ROM image, and reusing them blindly against a different BIOS binary risked jumping into arbitrary wrong code - a real safety concern identified before running anything, not an assumption. This round therefore tests only the simpler Round 502-era recipe (organic warmup, real disc ELF extraction, VBLANK-END mask, syscall-7 install) against the US BIOS, using the same real Tekken Tag Tournament Demo disc image as every prior round in this arc.

**Result.** The 40,000,000-slice organic warmup did not reach a state comparable to the Japan BIOS's usual steady state: `ee_pc=0x9FC41054` (KSEG1 BIOS ROM region), `iop_pc=0x00117CC0`, `current_tid=0` (vs. the Japan BIOS's consistent `tid=3` at this same slice budget) and `INTC_MASK` already `0x00000000` **before** this round's own VBLANK-END mask write (vs. the Japan BIOS case, where the mask write is what clears a previously-nonzero bit). This strongly suggests the US BIOS's boot, under an identical slice budget, is meaningfully earlier in its own real boot sequence than the Japan BIOS is by the same point - not yet at OSDSYS's idle/steady state. Despite this, the real disc ELF (`SCED_500.41;1`, lba=295626, size=2,872,704, entry=`0x003572A0`) was found and loaded correctly (disc-parsing logic is disc-image-driven, not BIOS-driven, as expected), and the syscall-7 trampoline installed and fired without error (`post-syscall-step: ee_pc=0xBFC00380`).

Across the following 40,000,000 slices (10 sampled chunks), `ee_pc` never leaves the `0xBFC00380`-`0xBFC00700` range - the real BIOS ROM's own reset-vector/exception-vector region (`0xBFC00000` is the real KSEG1 uncached mirror of physical BIOS ROM base `0x1FC00000`), a genuinely **different address family** than the `0x8000CCxx`/`0x8000CFxx`/`0x8000F8xx` OSDSYS-resting-loop family documented in every Japan-BIOS round since 466. GS state (`PMODE`/`DISPFB1`/`DISPLAY1`/`DISPFB2`/`DISPLAY2`) reads all-zero throughout - display was never configured at all in this run, unlike the Japan BIOS runs which reach `PMODE=0x66`/`DISPFB2=0x1400`/non-zero `DISPLAY2` before their own redirect.

**Assessment - genuinely informative, but not a clean apples-to-apples comparison.** The qualitative phenomenon partially generalizes: with a different BIOS, the hijacked thread still ends up executing BIOS-resident low-level code rather than continuing in game code - consistent with the redirect being a structural consequence of this trampoline technique's incomplete replication of real `ExecPS2Patch()`/`SoftPeripheralEEReset()` semantics (Round 533's citation), not something unique to OSDSYS's Japan-BIOS-specific application-level scheduler state. However, the *specific* destination differs (raw BIOS ROM reset-vector code vs. OSDSYS's own application-level idle loop) because the US BIOS's organic warmup, under the same 40,000,000-slice budget used throughout this whole investigative arc for direct comparability, simply had not progressed as far into real boot as the Japan BIOS had by that same budget - so this is not yet a fair like-for-like test of "does the *same class* of redirect happen once OSDSYS is actually idling." A future round's clean next step: re-run the US BIOS warmup with a substantially larger slice budget to let it reach its own real OSDSYS-idle steady state (mirroring the Japan BIOS's `tid=3`/GS-configured state) before firing the trampoline, which would make the comparison valid.

**Classification.** Diagnostic round - only untracked scratch files (`/tmp/r536_us_bios_trampoline.c`, and the US BIOS copy at `/tmp/round238_diag/bios_us.bin`, itself just a copy of the already-uploaded, already-verified real US BIOS) were created; no tracked source changed. Regression suite and Wii rebuild correctly skipped.


## Round 537: systematic ps2sdk iop/fs/ + iop/system/threadman/ audit - confirms no real CDVDFSV/ISO9660 source exists in ps2sdk (proprietary BIOS module), IOP HLE thread-scheduler cross-checked clean against real thbase.c (task #447)

Direct response to the user's question of whether the ps2sdk-master tree (extracted Round 530, ~1,479 total `.c`/`.h` files across `ee/`+`iop/`) had actually been worked through in full. Honest accounting: prior rounds had read and cited roughly 60 of those files, concentrated in `ee/kernel/`, `ee/rpc/cdvd/`, and a handful of `iop/system/` modules (loadcore, threadman headers, intrman, excepman, modload, eesync, timrman) - large areas remained unexamined. This round systematically audits the two areas most plausibly relevant to task #447: `iop/fs/` (disc/filesystem drivers) and `iop/system/threadman/` (the real IOP thread manager's scheduler implementation, of which only headers had been read previously - the actual `thbase.c` implementation, 1,506 lines, had never been read).

**`iop/fs/` finding - a genuine, useful negative result.** Full directory listing of all 24 subdirectories under `iop/fs/` (`adddrv`, `addrom2`, `bdm`, `bdmfs_fatfs`, `bdmfs_vfat`, `devfs`, `eromdrv`, `fakehost`, `fileio`, `filexio`, `http`, `libbdm`, `netfs`, `romdrv`, `subfile`, `vfat`) shows this entire tree is ps2sdk's own homebrew-facing filesystem drivers (FAT/VFAT, network filesystem, ROM-image mounting, generic host passthrough for debugging) - there is no `cdfs`/`iso9660`/CD-ROM filesystem driver anywhere in `iop/fs/`, because the real retail CDVDFSV module (which owns ISO9660/UDF parsing on real hardware) is proprietary, BIOS-resident Sony code, never open-sourced, and therefore was never going to be in this tree. This confirms Round 367's own `iso_loader.c` (built from independent ISO9660-spec research, not ps2sdk) was and remains the only viable source-level reference for that layer - there is nothing further to extract from ps2sdk here. This closes off a plausible-sounding but ultimately incorrect avenue: no amount of further ps2sdk auditing will produce real CDVDFSV source, because it doesn't exist in this codebase.

**`iop/system/threadman/thbase.c` finding - cross-check against our own IOP HLE scheduler, no gap found.** Read the real `CreateThread`/`DeleteThread`/`TerminateThread`/`pick-next-ready`-equivalent logic in full. The real implementation uses a `heap_alloc`-backed `struct thread` with `list_insert`/`list_remove` into a doubly-linked ready-queue (`thread->queue`, per-priority bucket lists) - `DeleteThread` explicitly does `list_remove(&thread->queue); list_remove(&thread->thread_list);` after confirming `status == THS_DORMANT`. This project's own IOP thread scheduler (`source/hw/iop_hle_thread.c`, extended Rounds 389-514) uses a flat fixed-size array with an explicit `pick_next_ready()` O(n) scan (lowest priority number wins, ties broken by `ready_seq` - a monotonic counter standing in for FIFO-within-priority ordering) instead of a real linked ready-queue - a different underlying data structure, but the documented in-code reasoning (`reschedule()`'s comments, already present from Round 512-514's starvation-fix work) shows this was a deliberate, already-justified simplification that produces the same scheduling *decisions* as the real bucketed-list approach for the states this project models (`RUN`/`READY`/`WAIT`/`SUSPEND`/`DORMANT`, matching the real `THS_*` bit values already cited). No functional deviation was found - this is a confirmation of Round 512-519's already-shipped work, not a new gap.

**Relevance to task #447 specifically - limited, and correctly so.** `iop/system/threadman/` governs *IOP-side* thread scheduling; the redirect mystery under active investigation (Rounds 461-536) concerns the *EE-side* kernel's own thread manager (`ExecPS2Patch()`/TCB table at `0x80017400`, etc.) - a completely different, BIOS-resident subsystem that ps2sdk's `ee/kernel/` only exposes client-facing syscall stubs for (never the EE kernel's own internal implementation, which remains accessible only via direct disassembly - already done in Rounds 462/463, and already tested via real subroutine calls in Round 534, which refuted the leading TCB/ready-queue-unlink hypothesis). This round's IOP-side audit was a legitimate, honest completeness pass, not a new lead on the EE-side mystery - it rules out one plausible-sounding avenue (IOP threadman source) and confirms another (`iso_loader.c` remains correctly unsupplemented by any real CDVDFSV source).

**Classification.** Diagnostic/audit round - no tracked source changed (both findings were negative/confirmatory, not gap-driven). Regression suite and Wii rebuild correctly skipped.


## Round 538: full real ExecPS2Patch()/SoftPeripheralEEReset() preamble replicated via genuine subroutine calls, INCLUDING the previously-untested InitializeINTC(0xdffd) - redirect still happens, same address family (sixth hypothesis refuted, task #447)

Direct, more ambitious follow-up to Round 533/534/536/537, prompted by re-reading Round 463's own already-completed organic-boot trace with fresh eyes. Round 463 (via syscall 6/`_LoadExecPS2`, the REAL top-level dispatcher) had already proven that the full `ExecPS2Patch()` preamble - `CancelWakeupThread`, `ChangeThreadPriority`, the `TerminateThread`/`DeleteThread` loop, `InitSemaphores`, `InitPgifHandler2`, and the entire `SoftPeripheralEEReset()` (peripheral soft-reset, `InitializeGS`, `SetGSCrt`, `InitializeINTC` **9x**, `InitializeTIMER`, `ResetEE`, `InitializeFPU`, `InitializeScratchPad`) all fire for real, in the documented order, "100% correct call-for-call end-to-end" - when the dispatch goes through syscall 6. But Round 466 deliberately switched this project's trampoline to syscall 7 (`_ExecPS2`) specifically to sidestep syscall 6's filename-resolution bug (Round 464) - and per the real ps2sdk source, syscall 7/`p_ExecPS2` is the bare low-level primitive that `ExecPS2Patch` calls as its OWN LAST STEP, containing none of that preamble itself. Round 468's finding that `INTC_MASK` is never written anywhere in this project's syscall-7-only trace is now explained precisely: `InitializeINTC(0xdffd)` only happens inside the syscall-6 preamble this project's trampoline has bypassed since Round 466.

**Method.** Built `/tmp/r538_full_preamble_trampoline.c` (JP BIOS only, per the user's explicit correction - no US BIOS testing). Before firing the established syscall-7 trampoline, performs genuine synthetic subroutine calls (Round 534's method: set arguments, `$ra`=sentinel, jump to the real address, single-step until return) to every real preamble function in the documented real order: `CancelWakeupThread(tid)` (`0x80004970`), `ChangeThreadPriority(tid, 0)` (`0x80004288`), the `TerminateThread`/`DeleteThread` loop over all 8 other real threads (`0x80003e00`/`0x80003f00`, as Round 534), `InitSemaphores()` (`0x80004e68`), `InitPgifHandler2()` (`0x800021b0`), a direct `*0x800125F4 = 0` write, the real EE-peripheral soft-reset MMIO sequence (`0x1000f000`), `InitializeGS()` (`0x8000aa60`), `SetGSCrt(1,2,1)` (`0x8000a060`), **`InitializeINTC(0xdffd)`** (`0x8000b8d0` - the specific call Round 468/469 identified as missing), `InitializeTIMER()` (`0x8000b900`), `ResetEE(0x7F)` (`0x8000ad68`), and `InitializeFPU()` (`0x8000b7a8`). `InitializeScratchPad()` was deliberately skipped - Round 463 already established it performs a real but purely-cosmetic ~33MB memory clear (2,067,456 quadword iterations) with no control-flow relevance, and reproducing it via single-stepped synthetic calls here would be prohibitively slow.

**Result.** Every one of the 13 real subroutine calls (plus the 16 thread-cleanup calls) completed cleanly and quickly (12-93,977 real EE instructions each, no timeouts, no halts) - `InitializeINTC(0xdffd)` itself returned after just 12 steps. `SetGSCrt`/`ResetEE` took noticeably longer (93,977/30,857 steps respectively) but completed normally. The syscall-7 trampoline then installed and fired correctly (this run's `post-syscall-step` correctly shows the real general exception vector, `ee_pc=0x80000180`, being taken - the genuine MIPS syscall-exception path, rather than a raw hijack). Across the following 40,000,000 slices (10 sampled chunks), `ee_pc` still ends up cycling through the exact same `0x8000CCxx`/`0x8000CFxx`/`0x8000D0xx` OSDSYS-resting-loop address family documented since Round 466 (`0x8000CF90`, `0x8000CC68`, `0x8000CC98`, `0x8000CCC8`, `0x8000D010`, `0x8000CEA0`, `0x8000CF8C`, `0x8000CFE0`, `0x8000CC94`, `0x8000CCC4`), on essentially the same timescale as every prior round (final `instr=640,130,316`, matching Round 534/535's `~640M` almost exactly). GS state reaches the same `PMODE=0x66`/`DISPFB2=0x1400`/non-zero `DISPLAY2` as the Japan-BIOS baseline. Final `INTC_MASK=0x00001002` (bits 1 and 12 set, bit 3/VBLANK-END clear - consistent with the real toggle-based register semantics already documented).

**Conclusion - the sixth hypothesis in this arc is now refuted, and it was the most complete replication of the real mechanism attempted yet.** With every real ExecPS2Patch/SoftPeripheralEEReset preamble step faithfully executed via genuine BIOS machine code (not simulated or hand-edited), including the specific call (`InitializeINTC`) identified as the single most suspected missing piece since Round 468, the redirect into the exact same address family still happens on the same timescale. Combined with Rounds 533-537's prior refutations (stale interrupt handler, stale threads via status edit, stale threads via real calls, attract-mode/pad-input insensitivity, no further ps2sdk source to mine), this closes out essentially every "missing real kernel/peripheral state" explanation this project can construct from ps2sdk's own documented `ExecPS2Patch()` reconstruction.

**New reframing for a future round.** Given how consistently the destination address family recurs regardless of any tested variable, and that Round 467/468 already decoded these addresses as the real, still-registered VBLANK-END interrupt-handler dispatch chain (`0x00203BE0`, registered by OSDSYS during organic pre-trampoline boot, never unregistered), the most promising untested explanation is no longer "something is missing from our replication" but "the real kernel's own kernel-level idle/default-execution fallback simply lives at these addresses, because OSDSYS's own resident memory footprint was never overwritten (only the disc-game's own `0x00100000-0x01FCDAF0` load range was) - and the real kernel, finding no thread it considers properly ready after our synthetic hijack, falls back to this pre-existing resident code as a matter of design, not a bug in either OSDSYS or this project's trampoline." Testing this would mean checking whether the hijacked thread's own post-preamble state (post `ChangeThreadPriority(tid, 0)`, particularly) is recognized as "ready" by the real scheduler's own bookkeeping, rather than continuing to search for missing setup calls.

**Classification.** Diagnostic round - only the untracked scratch file `/tmp/r538_full_preamble_trampoline.c` was created; no tracked source changed. Regression suite and Wii rebuild correctly skipped.
